summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a complex history including psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroids, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and heart failure was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest pain following a recent hospitalization for cellulitis. His dyspnea was multifactorial, attributed to fluid overload, restrictive lung disease, and discontinuation of CPAP after glaucoma surgery. He was treated with aggressive diuresis, which improved his volume status despite a transient rise in creatinine. Antibiotics were initiated empirically for possible pneumonia but discontinued due to negative cultures and lack of clear infection. His dexamethasone dose was tapered to reduce fluid retention, and CPAP was safely restarted with ophthalmology approval. Pain was managed with reduced opioid doses after an episode of sedation requiring Narcan. He stabilized on oral diuretics, insulin adjustments, and close electrolyte monitoring, and was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing steroid taper, CPAP use with weekly eye checks, and outpatient follow-up for ENT and rheumatology issues.
